November 12, 2026

House passes largest cuts to veterans' benefits on Veterans Day

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

The Republican-led House of Representatives passed H.R. 9237, described by Democrats as the largest cut to veterans' benefits in U.S. history, on Veterans Day. The bill would cut $57 billion from disability benefits for future veterans and nearly triple the VA streamlined refinancing fee. It cleared the floor in seconds by voice vote with no recorded roll call, leaving no public record of how individual lawmakers voted, and Democrats opposed the reductions during debate. The measure now goes to the Senate.

Pressure mounts on Hegseth over Arlington conduct and carrier conditions

tags: defence, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was reprimanded by an Army sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on Veterans Day after he and his entourage were seen laughing and joking, drawing condemnation from Major General Paul Eaton and the group VoteVets, which said it would work to protect the soldier involved. Separately, military families were reported to have confronted the Navy Secretary and other officials at a recent meeting after being told their relatives aboard the USS George W. Bush would not return home for the holidays because Iranian projectiles continue to threaten the carrier and more manpower is needed in the Middle East. Families described broken equipment and inadequate supplies aboard the ship. Calls for Hegseth's resignation or removal have grown.

Hegseth faces House impeachment vote over Iran war authorisation

tags: politics, legal, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

Hegseth is set to face an impeachment vote in the House over launching the war in Iran without congressional approval. Asked whether he should resign, former White House Press Secretary Katie Zachariah said he should not, calling him a successful war secretary and arguing history would credit both him and the president with preventing a nuclear-armed Iran. In the same interview she denied any rift between the president and Vice President JD Vance, and said questions over who placed Senator Dan Sullivan on the Alaska ballot were under investigation.

Trump directs enforcement at Democratic-run states and demands prosecutions

tags: politics, immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Beginning around 4:30 a.m., the president posted repeatedly on Truth Social, calling the Democratic Party corrupt and anti-American, asserting a new migrant caravan was approaching and that ICE had been informed there would be no leniency, and claiming Republicans lost the midterms because he was not on the ballot. In one post he asked Vice President JD Vance to focus attention on Democrat-run cities and states and alleged fraud there, adding that the administration does not need to deal with Iran. He also demanded the prosecution of six Democratic lawmakers, including Senators Elissa Slotkin and Mark Kelly, who had told service members not to follow unlawful orders, despite a grand jury previously refusing to indict them.

ICE contractor offers detainees $3,000 and a flight to self-deport

tags: immigration, surveillance
sources: @oafnation_actual

Geo Group, ICE's main private detention and monitoring contractor, sent alerts through the BI SmartLINK app used to supervise immigrants on GPS ankle monitors, promoting the self-deportation programme Project Homecoming. The notices offered airline tickets and $3,000 per person, including children, on arrival in a country of citizenship, legal residence, or a third country. Sources said it was the first time the programme had been promoted through the ankle monitor app. The alerts went out in late October and early November, ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

Carbon County weighs nuclear, gas and data center project with no public comment

tags: climate, tech, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Carbon County, Utah, was due to vote on a large nuclear, gas and data center development near Wellington at a meeting where the public would not be allowed to speak. Although presented as nuclear, developer Valar's own application states a gas plant would be the primary supply until any reactors operate, and no date is given for reactor construction. Valar has sued to bypass federal nuclear safety licensing, arguing it causes delays, while asking the county to approve reactors that have not passed that review. The application omits a water source, traffic study and noise limits, the landowner has not signed off, and the filing was made on October 27 with the meeting announced three days in advance.

Democrats probe Trump's top fundraiser over $800 million in contributions

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Democrats are investigating Meredith O'Rourke, the president's leading fundraiser, over roughly $800 million in contributions she has accepted on his behalf for projects including the White House ballroom. The inquiry was reported by the New York Times.

Republican infighting grows as party distances itself from Trump

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Republicans on Capitol Hill are increasingly at odds over the party's direction after the midterms, with many wanting the president to step back and stay quiet. Congressman Marlin Stutzman of Indiana, who narrowly held a heavily Republican district, has criticised Trump for repeated mistakes and for not listening to voters, and some Republicans want Stephen Miller removed. Trump's stated focus has shifted to building monuments over the coming years, according to Axios.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after reports of two affairs

tags: markets, tech
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual, @aaronparnas

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's president, chief executive and board member effective immediately, the company said, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO and Harvey Jones appointed the company's first board chair. In a November 8 memo Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife following reports of a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom U.S. officials believe worked for Chinese intelligence; a further report alleged a relationship with Nvidia healthcare vice president Kimberly Powell, and the Wall Street Journal reported the board was preparing to remove him. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and built it into a company holding an estimated 80% or more of the AI chip market. Shares fell more than 10% in premarket trading.

Paraguay central bank chief says collapsed bank harvested biometric data

tags: surveillance, markets
sources: @ericmoutsos

Paraguay's new central bank president told the Senate that a failed bank's real business was collecting the population's biometric data rather than banking, refusing some transactions unless customers submitted to facial recognition. He said the operation was connected to Israel and described losses in the region of $600 million. He told senators that risk in the financial system is more complex than assumed and extends to central banks and government decisions about where public money is held.

Eight dead in Brooklyn apartment building collapse

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

At least eight people, including two children, were killed and 18 others injured, among them four firefighters, when a three-storey apartment building collapsed next to a construction site in Brooklyn on Wednesday, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said. The building came down as crews excavated a neighbouring property, though investigators have not established a cause, and rescue teams searched the debris through Thursday in heavy rain. City records show inspectors halted demolition work at the neighbouring site in March over safety violations, that workers breached the order in April, and that construction was permitted to resume in May after corrections.

Four shot in active shooter incident in Washington DC

tags: policing
sources: @aaronparnas

At least four people were shot in an active shooter situation at the Vita Fitness in Logan Circle in Washington, D.C. The incident was reported on Thursday morning.

Zelensky reports fresh Starlink disruptions

tags: war, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Starlink service is again being disrupted. The outages were reported alongside other developments on Thursday morning.
